title: Decide which account owns chattic.us DNS and how environment subdomains are delegated
description:
A decision for Ryan, blocking the first real deploy into a new account. ChatticusWeb and ChatticusAuth take a hosted zone and an ACM certificate from ChatticusDns (bin/chatticus.ts), which today lives in the legacy account together with the chattic.us zone. A new account cannot deploy Web or Auth until it has its own zone or certificate.

Options: (1) keep the apex zone in one account (the management account is usual, or legacy until retired) and delegate dev./staging./auth-dev. style subdomains to a hosted zone in each environment account by NS records, each account issuing its own certificate; (2) move the whole zone to a new account; (3) one shared DNS account. Also decide the production hostnames (production currently serves hey.chattic.us), and note Google OAuth redirect URIs and the Cognito custom auth domains (auth-dev.chattic.us etc.) must be re-registered per environment.

Recommend (1) with subdomain delegation: least disturbance to the live zone, each environment account self-contained. Needs Ryan's answer.

comments.author: home
comments.text: DECIDED by Ryan (2026-09-30): move the chattic.us DNS to the management account. Facts gathered before recording (read-only, legacy account): the chattic.us zone has 20 record sets, all alias-to-CloudFront or ACM validation CNAMEs, NO MX/TXT (no email on the domain). Records: apex and www (marketing site, stack ChatticusMarketing, 4 records), dev., staging., hey. (web) and auth-dev., auth-staging., auth. (auth), plus two ACM validation CNAMEs for the marketing certificates. The domain is NOT registered in Route 53 in either account, so the name-server change is made at the outside registrar (Ryan only). Legacy also holds 10 other zones for other projects (out of scope). Consequences to plan for are on the new work card.
